# llms.txt — agent entry index for turvez

> Read AGENTS.md first (normative rules). This file only routes each
> task to the right doc — fetch only what the task needs.

## Start here (every task)

- AGENTS.md — layout, rules, traps, commands (normative). Q0: repo type first
  (`go.mod` = template public, `TURVEZ_PIN` = ops private).
- ARCHITECTURE.md — diagram, data flow, decisions
- README.md — quickstart, operator loop, examples
- docs/ops-repo.md — template vs ops split, lifecycle, tenancy map

## By task

- Write/edit a recipe: docs/writing-recipes.md (anatomy, engine-vs-handler
  table, what the engine allows here, traps, handler checklist)
- Task inputs/outputs: docs/handlers-reference.md (never invent task names)
- Observability/data rules: docs/observability.md (what is stored, prompt
  persistence, schema gates, retention, no gateway content logging)
- Client deployment model: docs/deployment-profiles.md (embedded vs managed
  vs multi-tenant, gateway placement, ownership)
- First run, in order, with the known traps: docs/first-run.md
- Flows as diagrams plus the format map: docs/workflows.md
- Client spine, engine-agnostic layout and migrations: docs/client-spine.md
- CLI/API for authoring: docs/agent-tools.md (prefer `--json`)
- Secrets: docs/secrets.md (names in JSON, values in env/age only)
- Alerts: docs/alerting.md (on_failure, DLQ watchdog, external probe)
- Tenancy/extract: docs/tenancy-evolution.md, docs/isolating-a-client.md
- Fresh checkout / install: scripts/setup.sh (check-only; --init scaffolds env), README Quickstart
- Validate a checkout: `make validate` (every engine with source: dagnats
  recipes + windmill lint, each skipped when absent; plus
  `scripts/test-decisions.sh` — every tree branch's artifact and gate exists)
  + `go test ./clients/` (structure, manifest/engine agreement, tenancy, jq
  expressions, secrets guard)
- New client fieldbook: clients/_template/FIELDBOOK.md (copy to clients/<client>/README.md)
- Client recipe template: clients/_template/{cron-job,webhook-pipeline,approval-flow-signal}.json
- Client layout and migrations: docs/client-spine.md (`clients/<client>/automation/<engine>/`)
- Personal automations: client `personal/` (same pipeline, you are the approver)
- Automate-anything skill: skills/turvez/SKILL.md (direct → confirm → build; link into your harness skills dir)
- Route any request: skills/turvez/references/decision-tree.md — the canonical
  tree, the interview protocol (read first, ≤3 branch-flipping questions, each
  with a recommendation, the answer recorded) and the defaults table
- Decision eval (behavioral): skills/turvez/evals/README.md — operator
  scenarios + a transcript grader; CI checks the fixtures, a model run is local
  (`python3 scripts/decision-eval.py --check --self-test | --grade <file>`)
- Client intake (interview + degustia tool picks): skills/turvez/references/client-intake.md
- Sandbox decision: docs/sandbox-policy.md (3 questions) + scripts/sandbox-run.sh for one-offs
- Where to execute (dagnats vs Dagu vs Windmill): docs/script-execution.md (decision tree)
- Migrating a client to Windmill: docs/migrate-to-windmill.md (mapping table)
  + `scripts/convert-to-windmill.py` (emits a skeleton with TODOs, never a port)
- Engine choice is per client (docs/client-spine.md#choosing-the-engine);
  **Windmill is the default** (`engines.json`), dagnats is the exception path:
  skills/turvez/references/windmill.md + docs/script-execution.md
  + `./scripts/check-windmill.sh` (lint gate, no worker)
- **Genkit is a capability, not an engine** (`docs/genkit.md`): a
  human-watched agent loop runs as a Genkit flow in a Go service, goai stays
  the only model path, tools go through Nango, and anything durable is a run
  in the client's engine. Never add `genkit` to `engines.json`. Scaffold:
  `scripts/new-agent-service.sh <client>` (plan, then `--apply --provider <slug>`);
  `scripts/check-agent-template.sh` compiles it in CI (pinned Genkit, temp module).
- Answering questions over client data: docs/retrieval.md — split documents
  (route-then-read: 2026 default is lexical for identifiers and hybrid BM25 + small
  dense + RRF + optional rerank of units for natural language; glossary expansion;
  routing unit = chunk that remembers its parent section/chapter; reading unit =
  parent, not chunk or whole chapter; hard token budget + candidate cap +
  calibrated refusal; rewrite is not a default rung — 0 or 1 cached rewrites unless
  the eval justifies it; vectors only behind an eval, inside Bleve) from systems of
  record (Nango proxy; Agent Sessions MCP only for an agent that chooses tools).
  Agent playbook: skills/turvez/references/retrieval.md
- Language policy: docs/language-policy.md — **script nodes are Go** in both
  engines. TypeScript/Python only for a Windmill WAC orchestrator that
  dispatches to Go scripts with `taskScript()`/`taskFlow()`. Gate:
  `./scripts/lint-scripts.sh` (compiles the Go, checks the bindings)
- Client isolation status: `./scripts/verify-isolation.sh` (reads runtime/target,
  read-only). Package one client for its own host: `scripts/extract-client.py`
  (prints the plan + commands, never executes them)

## Invariants (do not relearn these)

- Automation code = JSON in `clients/<client>/automation/dagnats/`; git is the
  source of truth, dagnats KV is a deployment target. New clients default to
  and `engine:` records it (docs/client-spine.md#choosing-the-engine).
- A client runs exactly one engine; `clients/<client>/client.yaml` decides.
- Workflow names are `<client><separator><wf>`; the separator and the name
  regex live in `naming.json` (single source of truth). Change them there,
  then `scripts/rename-workflows.sh --apply`.
- Durations in JSON accept integer nanoseconds or Go duration strings
  (`"30s"`); `$schema` is accepted but optional.
- Script nodes are Go in both engines; TypeScript/Python only for a Windmill
  WAC orchestrator that dispatches to Go scripts with `taskScript()`/`taskFlow()`
  (`docs/language-policy.md`, gate `./scripts/lint-scripts.sh`).
- Client SaaS keys/OAuth: authorise in Nango, never paste the value.
  `./scripts/nango-connect.sh <client> --provider <slug> --link --open` prints a
  30-minute link and the exact names; `clients/credentials_test.go` rejects a
  provider token in `env/` and a `Connection-Id` that is not the client, unless
  the id is recorded in `clients/<client>/nango/connections.json` (Connect UI
  assigns its own id — `docs/nango.md`).
- "RAG" is not a dependency: documents get a Go lexical index and an eval;
  tool data is called at its source. Nango MCP is for agent tool discovery,
  not for documents (`docs/retrieval.md`).
- New Go handler = last resort + tests + human review; no script exec.
